name: Kerberoasting (Rubeus /rc4opsec)
description: Request TGS tickets for all accounts with SPNs for offline cracking. /rc4opsec only roasts RC4-supporting accounts to avoid AES-only detection.

recommended.note: Find SPN accounts with PowerView first
CPTS card for cracking Kerberoast hashes
DCSync with cracked DA/privileged account creds
Lateral movement with cracked service account

notes: /rc4opsec only roasts accounts that support RC4. Newer CRTP labs have specific high-value service accounts as targets. Slides: Invoke-Kerberoast (BC-SECURITY Empire/PowerView) requests + extracts SPN hashes in one PowerShell cmdlet - an alternative to Rubeus kerberoast when you want to stay in PowerShell. After extracting, crack offline with John or Hashcat (TGS-REP = hashcat mode 13100).

defense.why_it_works: Any authenticated domain user can request a Kerberos service ticket (TGS) for any service with a registered SPN. The TGS is encrypted with the service account's NTLM hash (RC4 by default, or AES). Rubeus /rc4opsec requests only RC4 tickets (easier to crack). The encrypted blob is extracted and cracked offline with hashcat — no interaction with the target service required after the ticket is obtained.
defense.prerequisites: Any valid domain account (low-priv). Rubeus or impacket-GetUserSPNs. LDAP to enumerate SPNs. Kerberos TGS request access (port 88). Offline cracking capability (GPU + hashcat).
defense.impact: T1558.003 Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Kerberoasting. Service account password recovered offline. If the service account is a DA or has admin rights, immediate privilege escalation. Often service accounts have weak, old passwords — high crack rate.
defense.detection:
Event 4769 (Kerberos Service Ticket Requested) with Ticket Encryption Type = 0x17 (RC4-HMAC) for service accounts — legitimate service ticket requests in modern environments use AES (0x12/0x13). SIEM rule: 4769 with EncryptionType=0x17 AND ServiceName is a service account (not krbtgt). MDI 'Kerberoasting' detection. Bulk TGS requests for multiple SPNs from a single user/source in a short window.
Anomalous Kerberos activity: forged or stolen tickets by correlating malformed fields in logon events, RC4-encrypted TGTs, or TGS requests without corresponding TGT requests; suspicious processes accessing LSASS memory for ticket extraction (DET0522/AN1443).
Suspicious access to SSSD secrets database and Kerberos key material indicating ticket theft or replay; correlate anomalous file access with unusual Kerberos service ticket requests (AN1444).
Forging or replaying Kerberos tickets: monitor Unified Logs for anomalous kinit/klist activity and unusual authentication sequences (AN1445).
defense.artifacts: Event 4769: multiple TGS requests for service accounts with RC4 encryption type | MDI alert: 'Kerberoasting attack' | DC Kerberos log: ServiceName entries for SPN accounts | SIEM: 4769 RC4 burst from single source
defense.prevention:
Set long, random passwords on all service accounts (25+ chars) — makes cracking computationally infeasible. Use Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA) — 240-char random auto-rotating passwords, immune to Kerberoasting. Force AES encryption on service accounts (Supported Encryption Types = 0x18 AES only). MDI deployment. Remove unnecessary SPNs. Monitor Event 4769.
Active Directory Configuration: Reset KRBTGT account password twice (invalidates all golden tickets); rotate every 180 days.
Audit: Scan for insecure Kerberos configurations.
Credential Access Protection: On Linux, use SELinux to protect Kerberos key material.
Encrypt Sensitive Information: Enable AES Kerberos encryption instead of RC4.
Password Policies: Service accounts should have 25+ character passwords; use Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA).
Privileged Account Management: Limit domain admin to DCs only; restrict service account privileges.
defense.evasion: Request one ticket at a time with delays (--rc4opsec flag avoids 4769 AES downgrade noise). Request tickets only for high-value targets. Use /nowrap to avoid output format detection.
defense.misconfiguration: Service accounts have weak/old passwords with SPNs registered. RC4 encryption type not restricted. No gMSA usage. SPNs set on user accounts rather than machine accounts. MDI not deployed.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Kerberoastable accounts (SPN + weak password):
Get-ADUser -Filter {ServicePrincipalName -ne '$null'} -Properties ServicePrincipalName,PasswordLastSet,msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes
# PasswordLastSet: 2018 AND SupportedEncryptionTypes includes RC4 (0x17) → VULNERABLE

# Weak service account passwords:
# svc_sql: Password1  (set in 2018, never changed)
# Rubeus requests RC4 ticket → hashcat cracks in minutes
defense.secure_config:
# Use gMSA (auto-rotating 240-char passwords):
New-ADServiceAccount -Name 'svc_sql' -DNSHostName 'dc01.corp.local' -ManagedPasswordIntervalInDays 30
Install-ADServiceAccount 'svc_sql'
Set-Service -Name 'MSSQLSERVER' -Credential (Get-ADServiceAccountCredential 'svc_sql')

# Force AES-only encryption on service accounts:
Set-ADUser svc_sql -KerberosEncryptionType AES256
# OR via attribute editor: msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes = 16 (AES256 only)

# Rotate passwords for non-gMSA service accounts (25+ char random):
[System.Web.Security.Membership]::GeneratePassword(30, 5)
# Paste result into: Set-ADAccountPassword svc_old -Reset -NewPassword ...

# Alert on RC4 TGS requests:
# SIEM: EventID=4769 AND TicketEncryptionType=0x17 AND ServiceName NOT IN (krbtgt, *$) → ALERT

variations.label: Crack with hashcat (TGS-REP m13100 / AS-REP m18200)
